methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective radiomics study with 878 rectal cancer patients split 8:2 for training/test; one random split from 10 permutations reported. Multivariate logistic regression for clinical features; LASSO feature selection with appropriate preprocessing (Mann-Whitney U, Spearman correlation cutoff >0.9). However, significant methodological limitation acknowledged: distant metastasis diagnosis based on imaging (CT/ultrasound) rather than pathological confirmation. ROI delineation blinded with ICC >0.9 achieved. No external validation; single-center study with acknowledged generalizability concerns.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Diagnostic/prognostic prediction model study (LoE 4). Addresses clinically important question of preoperative distant metastasis detection to guide treatment planning. However, lack of histopathological confirmation of metastasis (imaging-only diagnosis) limits evidentiary strength. Model performance adequate (test AUC 0.749 for integrated model) but not practice-changing without external validation and prospective confirmation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods generally well-reported (DenseNet201 architecture, LASSO parameters, ICC thresholds, imaging protocols). Follows modified TRIPOD for prediction models but lacks some checklist items regarding model equations and calibration. No mention of data, code, or model availability. Training/test split methodology partially described (10 random splits, one selected) without pre-specified criteria for split selection.

novelty_literature.justification: First application of deep learning radiomics on CETRUS for distant metastasis prediction in rectal cancer; however, radiomics/deep learning approaches to metastasis prediction already established with CT/MRI. DenseNet201 transfer learning from ImageNet is standard practice. Clinical findings (elevated platelets, alcohol) are known risk factors. Model architecture and methodology incremental rather than novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear, well-organized manuscript with logical flow from motivation through methods, results, and discussion. Acknowledges major limitations transparently: imaging-only diagnosis, single-center, no external validation, short follow-up. Figures effectively illustrate workflow and nomogram. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within broader radiomics literature. Minor: some dense statistical presentation but overall publication-ready.

key_strengths: Novel application of deep learning radiomics to CETRUS imaging for metastasis prediction; clinically practical given ultrasound availability and lack of radiation
Large single-center cohort (n=878) with systematic feature selection methodology combining statistical tests and LASSO regularization
Comprehensive performance metrics (AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV) reported for all models with training/test stratification
Transparent acknowledgment of methodological limitations including imaging-only diagnosis, single-center design, and overfitting concerns (TDUS model)
key_concerns: Critical limitation: distant metastasis defined by imaging rather than pathological gold standard, risking misclassification of benign lesions and missed occult metastases
Single-center retrospective design with no external validation; generalizability unknown
Train-test split methodology unclear: states 10 random splits created, but final split selected without pre-specified criteria, risking selection bias
TDUS model shows substantial overfitting (AUC 0.935 train, 0.586 test); authors acknowledge but remediation strategies not implemented
No data, code, or model availability statement; reproducibility limited
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound but limited retrospective study with major validation concerns. Strong clinical question and transparent limitation discussion prevent rejection, but imaging-only diagnosis and lack of external validation require major revision before publication at Tier 3.
